```{r}
#| label: or-setup
fmt_tbl <- function(df, right = NULL) {
  right <- union(names(df)[vapply(df, is.numeric, TRUE)], right)
  flextable::flextable(df) |>
    flextable::fontsize(size = 9, part = "all") |>
    flextable::align(align = "center", part = "header") |>
    flextable::align(j = setdiff(names(df), right), align = "left", part = "body") |>
    flextable::align(j = right, align = "right", part = "body") |>
    flextable::colformat_int(big.mark = "") |>
    flextable::padding(padding.top = 1, padding.bottom = 1, part = "all") |>
    flextable::set_table_properties(layout = "autofit", width = 1)
}
read_tbl <- function(f) readr::read_csv(file.path("../03.outputs/TBL", f), show_col_types = FALSE, col_types = readr::cols(.default = "c"))
```

Online Resources for the article submitted to Climatic Change. Each item is cited in the article by its number. The code that produced every table and figure is in the article's source file in the repository named in the Data availability statement.

**Online Resource 1** Net emissions, five-year mean and reduction for British Columbia under three accounts, 2017 to 2024, from the provincial lines of the national inventory. The five-year mean was that of 2012 to 2016. The burned area share was the province's share of the area burned in Canada. The threshold account left out the natural disturbance line only in years that passed both the national and the provincial test.

```{r}
fmt_tbl(read_tbl("tbl-bc.csv"))
```

**Online Resource 2** The emission reduction of each account from 10,000 Monte Carlo draws with the published model interval on every annual value. The mean and standard deviation are those of the draws, and the 5th and 95th percentiles bound the 90 per cent interval. The relative half width is half the distance between those percentiles over the mean, the 90 per cent confidence interval of Equation 8, and the adjustment factor is that half width times 0.524417 over 1.645006, the share of the reduction withheld. Both are printed only where the mean reduction is positive.

```{r}
fmt_tbl(read_tbl("tbl-uncertainty.csv"))
```
